title: Huffman v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC found the filing styled as an appeal judicially out of order and remanded it to Tennessee Valley Presbytery for adjudication as a complaint at its next stated meeting. If Presbytery fails to act or denies the complaint, it may be carried to the SJC.
first_summary: Huffman appealed Presbytery’s disposition of his confession under BCO 38-1. The SJC found the appeal judicially out of order because the case began and was nearly completed before BCO 38-1 changed the available review from complaint to appeal. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the filing as a complaint under the former rule.
summary: A filing challenging Presbytery’s handling of Huffman’s BCO 38-1 confession was styled as an appeal under a newly amended rule. The SJC found it judicially out of order because the case began and was nearly completed when the former rule provided review by complaint, and retroactive application would be unfair. It remanded for Presbytery to adjudicate the filing as a complaint at its next stated meeting; denial or failure to act permits review by the SJC. No merits issue was decided.
